status: Scoped incoming WalletConnect Polkadot signing and request-lifecycle checks accepted locally; pairing, real relay/device and release gates remain open.
behavior: Incoming Polkadot signing uses a current acknowledged, unexpired approved namespace containing the exact method/chain/decoded account tuple. Proposal grants and ordinary website permissions cannot substitute for the session grant. Chain-scoped namespaces and SS58 aliases are supported.

Snapshot the original event, canonical HTTP(S) requester origin, peer identity, expiry, namespaces and session revision. Reject invalid verification, unsupported methods, malformed raw hex, and extrinsics whose nested account or genesis prefix disagrees with the request.

Use private UUID queue identities and an active topic/remote-ID owner. The same remote ID on different sessions does not collide in the application queue. Registered local, external and mobile Substrate signers use existing exact-key/payload/signature checks.

Retain the exact private queued request through remote response in an internal signing capsule. Its final validator rechecks incoming session, signer/key/mobile session, Substrate metadata/network and payload after queue completion, without relying on a queue entry already intentionally removed.

An EVM completion guard also checks its captured context immediately before the handler responds. Explicit request deadlines and installed-SDK session_request_expire events veto both protocols; the SDK event contains only a numeric ID, so that ID is conservatively retired across topics for this client lifetime.

Session deletion, expiry and local disconnect retire topics before asynchronous relay cleanup; updates and extensions increment revisions. Concurrent initialization shares one promise/client/listener set, with retry after initialization failure.

Signing receipt no longer silently extends session expiry. Each protocol handler checks approved namespaces; unsupported requests cannot keep a session alive. The existing mobile grant validator is extracted into a shared module with only symbol/error-label changes.

focused.scope: Actual handlers, queues, context checks and approval paths with public unfunded development keys and actual signatures; SDK initialization/relay transport and providers are controlled fixtures.

validation.lintScope: All changed production/test TypeScript files; not whole-repository lint.

browser.scope: Existing intercepted shared EVM/Substrate popup fixtures on the rebuilt development artifact; not a live incoming WalletConnect or mobile journey. Inherited software-rendering harness records two completed frames per capture.

independentReview.mode: Read-only source/diff review; reviewer did not edit or run web tests.

initialFinding.finding: The completed Polkadot request rechecked only the incoming session before reply. Account/key/mobile-session or metadata/network changes in the queue-completion microtask could still release a signature.

independentReview.finalAssessment: No remaining scoped blocker found in the revised source.
reviewedConclusions: Approved namespaces authorize the exact method/chain/account; proposal fields and ordinary site grants do not authorize the incoming request.

The internal signWalletConnect capsule retains the exact private queued request synchronously on the session-admission branch. Its final validator covers session/deadline, Substrate network/metadata, current account/key mapping and outgoing mobile session after settlement, without incorrectly requiring the completed queue entry.
responseRequest calls SDK respond without another application await before dispatch. Shared request validity rejects malformed/expired deadlines and recorded SDK expirations in both protocol paths.
Detached event/context, private UUID plus active tuple ownership, session tombstones and shared initialization are coherent; shared mobile helper extraction preserves behavior.
limits: Scoped source review, not independent relay/device/runtime execution.
Root executes and records the actual tests and artifact qualification separately.

finalFixtureOnlyDelta.change: Initialize the expiry reader in the older test mock; production source is byte-identical to reviewed application.

preservedDiagnostics.note: Initial incoming-session authorization, revocation, completion and genesis regressions against the accepted base.
External-signature negative fixture expected false while the established API rejects; corrected the fixture, not the authorization check.
Concurrent initialization reproduced two SDK clients before singleton initialization was implemented.
EVM session revision could change in queue completion before the outgoing result was released.

Intermediate full/type/lint/build/package/browser qualification passed, but independent review found a remaining completed-request account/network/mobile validation gap. This candidate was not accepted.
Reproduced all four account/key/network/metadata completion mutations, outgoing-mobile revocation, invalid/expired explicit deadlines and EVM deadline admission.
An older EVM test mock lacked the new expiry reader; final fixture-only follow-up initializes it and reruns all qualification.

Early typecheck diagnostics preserve a missing required AccountJson fixture field, hex-signature fixture types, and deferred-promise fixture types. Scoped lint import-order failures were corrected. Final checks all exit zero.

limits: The final check occurs immediately before handing the response to the SDK. It cannot recall a signature/result already handed to transport, or an EVM transaction already broadcast. No real relay, remote signer, cross-app or physical-device journey is qualified here.

SDK request-expiry events contain no topic; matching numeric IDs are conservatively vetoed across topics for this client lifetime. Expired pending screens are blocked when approval is attempted; proactive popup dismissal is not claimed.

Raw Substrate signatures bind their wrapped bytes, not a blockchain. Their session chain is an approved transport route. Extrinsic genesis checks bind the requested CAIP prefix; live runtime metadata and chain execution/finality are not established by these fixtures.
Removing automatic session extension means a session expires at its current approved expiry unless separately extended; this checkpoint does not add a session-renewal UI.
Mobile pairing negotiation and account mapping, other protocol mappings, durable authorization/session storage failure/restart behavior and physical accessibility remain separate gates.
Final historical upgrades/private-chain reruns and production bundle/publication remain open. Eighteen inherited skips remain skips; the packaged archive is a development artifact.
